newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany unlikely to meet EMU criteria - SPD official.
newsitem.headline: Germany unlikely to meet EMU criteria - SPD official.

text.p: A member of the opposition Social Democrats predicted Germany would probably miss the fiscal criteria for European monetary union (EMU) and called for a strict application of the entry criteria.

Heinz Schleusser, finance minister of the state of North Rhine-Westphalia, told the weekly Die Zeit that he did not expect Germany to exactly hit the target for the public budget deficit of three percent of gross domestic product.

Even if state and local governments maintain budget discipline, "net new borrowing would run to 117 billion marks this year," he said in an interview due to appear on Thursday. "But 3.0 would correspond with 110 billion marks."
Schleusser also supported a strict application of the deficit target, and criticised Bonn Finance Minster Theo Waigel for insisting Germany would make the 3.0 percent goal.

"Anyone who allows room for manoeuvre now, slips inevitably and lands at 4.0 or higher," he said. "Whoever softens (the criteria) now, strengthens the feeling that the euro will be no equal replacement for the mark."
Waigel should be graded against his promises to hit the 3.0 target, Schleusser said. "In spite of everything, he says again and again: three is 3.0. He should be measured against that."

Schleusser said the SPD would resist the coalition's efforts to cut the solidarity tax surcharge, dimming chances of a deal on government tax reforms in the mediation committee of the upper and lower houses of parliament.
"Against the SPD's two thirds majority in the upper house the government is powerless," he said.
